thread.title: Spotify: How Apple, Amazon, and Others Could Affect Its Plans

title: Spotify: How Apple, Amazon, and Others Could Affect Its Plans
text:
David Marino-Nachison July 9, 2018 11:59 a.m. ET
It should be a good time to invest in streaming music—and Spotify Technology (SPOT) is in the best position to benefit, according to MKM Partners. But what about the competition?
In a Monday note, the analysts at MKM—who have a “buy” rating and a $200 price target, 14% above current levels and ahead of FactSet’s consensus target, on the shares—examined Spotify’s major competitors in streaming music, suggesting a range of possible outcomes: Newsletter Sign-up
• Apple (AAPL): “We think Apple will be a large player for subscription services, but that its base will be confined to a portion of those consumers still wedded to iTunes,” the analysts wrote. “We expect zero traction outside of iOS, which itself is only 15-17% of world-wide smartphone users. Even if the company converts half its U.S. smartphone share to Apple Music (which would be pulling a rabbit out of a hat in our view), this is only 20% of the domestic market and for Apple this would just be shifting download dollars to subscription dollars.”
• Amazon.com (AMZN): “Will Amazon “play nice” with other music services on Alexa? We think yes, at least with Spotify,” the analysts wrote. “The company’s mission ‘to be Earth’s most customer-centric company’ is not fulfilled by banning highly popular consumer services from its platform. The company has had numerous squabbles with Apple and Google and ongoing issues with YouTube, but these are over larger corporate disagreements and mostly related to terms in those companies’ app stores. Spotify represents no such conflict for Amazon.”
• Alphabet-owned (GOOGL) Google: “While the rise of YouTube has been great for consumers and for Google, participation of the music industry is nowhere close to proportionate and labels have been vocal on this issue,” the analysts wrote. “We think the recent agreement on interactive rights necessary to launch YouTube Music are seen by labels as ‘something is better than nothing,’ but YouTube is still viewed as a problem area for the industry.”
• Pandora Media (P): “The shift to on-demand streaming forced the company to reverse course strategically,” the analysts wrote. “In order to obtain the necessary interactive rights ... Pandora had to negotiate directly with labels and publishers. This meant settling past disputes (writing big checks) and absorbing higher licensing costs. A business model that always made technology investment challenging got worse and the company was years behind in developing an on-demand platform. ... We think the opportunity for Pandora to be a large platform on a global scale has passed.”
Technology has made it easier to listen to music wherever, whenever and however consumers wish—but it’s taken the industry a long time to construct business models that match the technology, according to MKM. More About Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50
“Like other media, the incumbent structure of the music industry was shaped largely by its consumption, distribution and promotion model,” they wrote. “When consumption and distribution of media fundamentally change, so does industry structure. We think the music industry is in the early stages of transformation.”
MKM also examined the competitive landscape before Spotify’s public offering earlier this year . And last month, we shared another viewpoint on the relative strengths Spotify’s competitors may have .
All of the companies mentioned in this story are Barron’s Next 50 components.
